--[[
	Sites  -  the points a part is broken around (Break = "Shards"): the engine cuts one shard per point,
	the solid nearer to it than to any other (a Voronoi cell). Numbers only. Points and `hit` are
	offsets in the part's own space; `random` gives 0..1, the same sequence the same points.
	  Sites.count(size, pieces) -> points for a part (held to Sites.MAX and LEAST_VOLUME; under 2: no cut)
	  Sites.even(size, count, random), Sites.aroundHit(size, count, hit, random) -> { Vector3 }
	  Sites.hitIn(size, point), Sites.face(size, point) -> axis, side (of faces about as near, the largest)
	  Sites.faceAxes(axis), Sites.underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, depth), Sites.alongFace(axis, u, v, normal)
	  Sites.probes(size, axis, side, u, v, reach) -> places under a face to ask a Force's field at
	  Sites.cracks(size, count, hit, reach, random, options) -> { Vector3 }, strike, split
	      Cracked ground: a crust's points in rings around the hit (rubble, forking cracks, long
	      pieces past the reach); a crust of LEAST_LAYERED or more gets two staggered points a place.
	      strike = { origin, normal, reach, crust }; split = { inCrust, inBase }, the two points that
	      cut crust from base (nil for a part too thin). options: face = { axis, side }; fill (the
	      face is cut whatever the rings give it); crust (keep a first cut's); line = { path, reach,
	      seed } (a Linear Force's split: places along the path, one layout for every part it crosses).
	  Sites.LAYERS, Sites.RUN_ON, Sites.sequence(seed) -> random, Sites.seedAt(point) -> seed
]]

local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)

local Sites = {}

Sites.MAX = 240
Sites.LAYERS = 2
-- The average shard is never smaller than this, in cubic studs: a half-stud cube.
local LEAST_VOLUME = 0.125
-- Points stay within this share of the box, clear of its faces.
local INSET = 0.95
-- aroundHit: the share of points near the hit, their reach (share of the longest edge) and how
-- strongly they crowd toward it (under 1 crowds).
local NEAR_SHARE = 0.7
local NEAR_REACH = 0.4
local CROWDING = 0.6

local AXES = { "X", "Y", "Z" }
local SIDES = { 1, -1 }
-- face: a face this much farther off than the nearest still counts as near as it.
local FACE_SLACK = 0.25
-- cracks: the share of points that is rubble at the hit, and how far out it lies (share of reach).
local RUBBLE_SHARE = 0.1
local RUBBLE_REACH = 0.12
-- Bands crowd toward the hit: band i of n ends at (i / n) ^ BAND_CROWDING of the reach.
local BAND_CROWDING = 1.3
-- A crack forks where its piece would be this many times wider than deep.
local FORK_AT = 2.4
-- How unevenly cracks leave the hit, and how far a piece's point strays across its band.
local UNEVEN = 0.3
local ACROSS = 0.3
-- Past the reach the cracks run on as long pieces, to this many times the reach.
local RUN_ON = 1.9
Sites.RUN_ON = RUN_ON
local MOST_BANDS = 14
-- The crust: this share of the reach, at least LEAST_CRUST studs, at most CRUST_SHARE of the part;
-- with no room for that, no base.
local CRUST_REACH_SHARE = 0.075
local LEAST_CRUST = 0.5
local CRUST_SHARE = 0.45
-- A crust this thick is cut in two layers; a thinner one would give flakes.
local LEAST_LAYERED = 1
-- How deep each layer's points lie, as shares of the crust.
local UPPER = 0.28
local LOWER = 0.72
-- How far a place's two points stand to either side, as a share of the way to the nearest place.
local STAGGER = 0.3

function Sites.sequence(seed)
	local state = seed % 2147483647
	return function()
		state = (state * 48271 + 11) % 2147483647
		return state / 2147483647
	end
end

function Sites.seedAt(point)
	return math.floor(math.abs(point.X * 31.7 + point.Y * 57.3 + point.Z * 17.1) * 1000) % 2147483646 + 1
end

function Sites.count(size, pieces)
	local wanted = math.floor(math.min(pieces, Sites.MAX))
	local room = math.floor(size.X * size.Y * size.Z / LEAST_VOLUME)
	return math.max(math.min(wanted, room), 0)
end

local function anywhere(size, random)
	return Vector3.new((random() - 0.5) * size.X, (random() - 0.5) * size.Y, (random() - 0.5) * size.Z) * INSET
end

function Sites.even(size, count, random)
	local points = table.create(count)
	for index = 1, count do
		points[index] = anywhere(size, random)
	end
	return points
end

function Sites.hitIn(size, point)
	local half = size / 2
	return Vector3.new(math.clamp(point.X, -half.X, half.X), math.clamp(point.Y, -half.Y, half.Y), math.clamp(point.Z, -half.Z, half.Z))
end

function Sites.aroundHit(size, count, hit, random)
	local points = table.create(count)
	local reach = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z) * NEAR_REACH
	local near = math.floor(count * NEAR_SHARE)
	for index = 1, count do
		if index > near then
			points[index] = anywhere(size, random)
		else
			local direction = Vector3.new(random() - 0.5, random() - 0.5, random() - 0.5)
			if direction.Magnitude < 1e-4 then
				direction = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
			end
			local offset = hit + direction.Unit * (reach * random() ^ CROWDING)
			points[index] = Sites.hitIn(size, offset) * INSET
		end
	end
	return points
end

-- How far `point` lies from the face of the box across `axis` on `side`, as a rectangle.
local function faceDistance(size, point, axis, side)
	local squared = (point[axis] - side * size[axis] / 2) ^ 2
	for _, other in ipairs(AXES) do
		if other ~= axis then
			local past = math.max(math.abs(point[other]) - size[other] / 2, 0)
			squared += past * past
		end
	end
	return math.sqrt(squared)
end

function Sites.face(size, point)
	local bestAxis, bestSide = "Y", 1
	local least, bestArea = math.huge, 0
	for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
		local area = size.X * size.Y * size.Z / size[axis]
		for _, side in ipairs(SIDES) do
			local distance = faceDistance(size, point, axis, side)
			local clearlyNearer = distance < least * (1 - FACE_SLACK)
			local asNearAndLarger = distance <= least * (1 + FACE_SLACK) and area > bestArea
			if clearlyNearer or asNearAndLarger then
				bestAxis, bestSide = axis, side
				least, bestArea = distance, area
			end
		end
	end
	return bestAxis, bestSide
end

-- The two axes a face normal to `axis` lies in.
local function faceAxes(axis)
	if axis == "X" then
		return "Y", "Z"
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return "X", "Z"
	end
	return "X", "Y"
end

-- A point of the part from its place (u, v) in a face and its depth under that face.
local function underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, depth)
	local along = side * (size[axis] / 2 - depth)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(along, u, v)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(u, along, v)
	end
	return Vector3.new(u, v, along)
end

-- The angle after `angle` in a ring of angles that goes once round.
local function nextIn(angles, index)
	local following = angles[index % #angles + 1]
	if following <= angles[index] then
		following += 2 * math.pi
	end
	return following
end

-- The ring's places (u, v) around (hitU, hitV), for `count` points. inside(u, v) keeps a place.
local function rings(count, hitU, hitV, reach, random, inside)
	local places = {}
	local function add(u, v)
		-- A place outside the part cuts nothing: it is left out, never pushed onto the edge.
		if inside(u, v) then
			table.insert(places, { u, v })
		end
	end

	local rubble = math.floor(count * RUBBLE_SHARE)
	for _ = 1, rubble do
		local angle = random() * 2 * math.pi
		local radius = reach * RUBBLE_REACH * math.sqrt(random())
		add(hitU + math.cos(angle) * radius, hitV + math.sin(angle) * radius)
	end

	-- More cracks leave the hit the more pieces there are to make.
	local cracksAtHit = math.clamp(math.round(math.sqrt(count) * 0.9), 6, 16) + math.floor(random() * 3)
	local angles = {}
	local turn = random() * 2 * math.pi
	for index = 1, cracksAtHit do
		angles[index] = turn + (index - 1 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * UNEVEN) / cracksAtHit * 2 * math.pi
	end

	local function edges(band, bands)
		local inner = reach * (RUBBLE_REACH + (1 - RUBBLE_REACH) * ((band - 1) / bands) ^ BAND_CROWDING)
		local outer = reach * (RUBBLE_REACH + (1 - RUBBLE_REACH) * (band / bands) ^ BAND_CROWDING)
		return inner, outer
	end
	-- The points `bands` bands take, forks counted in, with the long pieces past the reach.
	local function cost(bands)
		local total = 0
		local across = cracksAtHit
		for band = 1, bands do
			local inner, outer = edges(band, bands)
			if math.pi * (inner + outer) / across > FORK_AT * (outer - inner) then
				across *= 2
			end
			total += across
		end
		return total + across
	end
	local bands = 1
	while bands < MOST_BANDS and cost(bands + 1) <= count - rubble do
		bands += 1
	end

	for band = 1, bands + 1 do
		local inner, outer = edges(math.min(band, bands), bands)
		if band > bands then
			inner = reach
			outer = reach * RUN_ON
		end
		local depth = outer - inner
		if band <= bands and math.pi * (inner + outer) / #angles > FORK_AT * depth then
			local forked = {}
			for index, angle in ipairs(angles) do
				table.insert(forked, angle)
				table.insert(forked, angle + (nextIn(angles, index) - angle) * (0.5 + (random() - 0.5) * 0.3))
			end
			angles = forked
		end
		for index, angle in ipairs(angles) do
			-- A piece's point sits midway between its two cracks.
			local along = (angle + nextIn(angles, index)) / 2
			local radius = (inner + outer) / 2 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * ACROSS * depth
			add(hitU + math.cos(along) * radius, hitV + math.sin(along) * radius)
		end
	end
	return places
end

-- About `count` places over a face (half-lengths halfU, halfV): a grid of near-square cells, each
-- place off its cell's middle by up to SPREAD_JITTER.
local SPREAD_JITTER = 0.25
local function spread(count, halfU, halfV, random)
	local columns = math.clamp(math.round(math.sqrt(count * halfU / halfV)), 1, count)
	local rows = math.max(math.round(count / columns), 1)
	local places = {}
	for row = 1, rows do
		for column = 1, columns do
			local u = (2 * (column - 0.5 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * SPREAD_JITTER) / columns - 1) * halfU * INSET
			local v = (2 * (row - 0.5 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * SPREAD_JITTER) / rows - 1) * halfV * INSET
			table.insert(places, { u, v })
		end
	end
	return places
end

-- A crust's points for its places: one at its middle, or a high and a low one staggered when it is
-- thick enough. lay(u, v, depth) -> Vector3.
local function layered(places, crust, halfU, halfV, random, lay)
	local points = {}
	if crust < LEAST_LAYERED then
		for _, place in ipairs(places) do
			table.insert(points, lay(place[1], place[2], crust / 2))
		end
		return points
	end
	local limitU, limitV = halfU * INSET, halfV * INSET
	for index, place in ipairs(places) do
		local gap = 2 * math.max(halfU, halfV)
		for other, candidate in ipairs(places) do
			if other ~= index then
				gap = math.min(gap, math.sqrt((candidate[1] - place[1]) ^ 2 + (candidate[2] - place[2]) ^ 2))
			end
		end
		local angle = random() * 2 * math.pi
		local du = math.cos(angle) * gap * STAGGER
		local dv = math.sin(angle) * gap * STAGGER
		table.insert(points, lay(math.clamp(place[1] + du, -limitU, limitU), math.clamp(place[2] + dv, -limitV, limitV), crust * UPPER))
		table.insert(points, lay(math.clamp(place[1] - du, -limitU, limitU), math.clamp(place[2] - dv, -limitV, limitV), crust * LOWER))
	end
	return points
end

Sites.faceAxes = faceAxes
Sites.underFace = underFace

function Sites.alongFace(axis, u, v, normal)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(normal, u, v)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(u, normal, v)
	end
	return Vector3.new(u, v, normal)
end

-- How far under the face a probe lies.
local PROBE_DEPTH = 0.5

function Sites.probes(size, axis, side, u, v, reach)
	local points = { underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, PROBE_DEPTH) }
	for ring = 1, 3 do
		local radius = reach * ring * 0.3
		for step = 1, 8 do
			local angle = step / 8 * 2 * math.pi
			table.insert(points, underFace(size, axis, side, u + math.cos(angle) * radius, v + math.sin(angle) * radius, PROBE_DEPTH))
		end
	end
	return points
end

function Sites.cracks(size, count, hit, reach, random, options)
	local face = options and options.face
	local fill = options and options.fill
	local line = options and options.line
	local axis, side = Sites.face(size, hit)
	if face then
		axis, side = face.axis, face.side
	end
	local uAxis, vAxis = faceAxes(axis)
	local halfU, halfV = size[uAxis] / 2, size[vAxis] / 2
	local hitU, hitV = hit[uAxis], hit[vAxis]
	local function inside(u, v)
		return math.abs(u) < halfU * INSET and math.abs(v) < halfV * INSET
	end

	local crustReach = reach
	if line then
		reach = line.reach
		crustReach = line.path.length
		-- The crust is cut off its base under the split's middle.
		local middle = Fissure.at(line.path, 0.5)
		hitU, hitV = middle[uAxis], middle[vAxis]
	else
		-- The rings are drawn in to the face: none of the points is spent beyond its far corner.
		local farthest = math.sqrt((math.abs(hitU) + halfU) ^ 2 + (math.abs(hitV) + halfV) ^ 2)
		reach = math.min(reach, farthest / 1.2)
		crustReach = reach
	end

	local thickness = size[axis]
	local crust = math.min(math.max(crustReach * CRUST_REACH_SHARE, LEAST_CRUST), thickness * CRUST_SHARE)
	if options and options.crust then
		crust = options.crust
	end
	local split = nil
	if crust >= LEAST_CRUST then
		-- One point in the crust and one under it, in line: the cut between them is flat.
		local apart = math.min(crust, thickness - crust) / 2
		local u = math.clamp(hitU, -halfU * INSET, halfU * INSET)
		local v = math.clamp(hitV, -halfV * INSET, halfV * INSET)
		split = {
			inCrust = underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, crust - apart),
			inBase = underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, crust + apart),
		}
	else
		crust = thickness
	end
	if crust >= LEAST_LAYERED then
		count = math.min(count, Sites.MAX // Sites.LAYERS)
	end

	local seed = math.floor(random() * 2147483645) + 1
	local places = {}
	local spare = count
	if line then
		local along = Fissure.places(count, line.path, reach, RUN_ON, Sites.sequence(line.seed or seed), function(position)
			return inside(position[uAxis], position[vAxis])
		end)
		for index, position in ipairs(along) do
			places[index] = { position[uAxis], position[vAxis] }
		end
		spare = 2
	else
		-- Places outside the part are lost: the rings are drawn again from the same numbers until about
		-- as many are kept as asked.
		places = rings(count, hitU, hitV, reach, Sites.sequence(seed), inside)
		local asked = count
		for _ = 1, 16 do
			if #places >= count * 0.95 then
				break
			end
			asked = math.ceil(asked * 1.12)
			local more = rings(asked, hitU, hitV, reach, Sites.sequence(seed), inside)
			if #more > count then
				break
			end
			places = more
		end
	end
	if fill and #places < 2 then
		places = spread(math.max(spare, 2), halfU, halfV, Sites.sequence(seed))
	end
	local points = layered(places, crust, halfU, halfV, Sites.sequence(seed + 7), function(u, v, depth)
		return underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, depth)
	end)

	local strike = {
		origin = underFace(size, axis, side, hitU, hitV, 0),
		normal = underFace(Vector3.new(2, 2, 2), axis, side, 0, 0, 0),
		reach = reach,
		crust = crust,
	}
	if line then
		strike.path = line.path
	end
	return points, strike, split
end

return Sites

--[[
	SkinDisplay: what is left intact of a skin (Reactor/Layers: a thin mesh part or union lying on a
	ground) while that ground has open cracks: a copy of the skin with the wounds taken out, while the
	skin itself is hidden. A skin has any outline, so the rest cannot be drawn as boxes (Reactor/GroundDisplay).

	The copy is the engine's (Reactor/Shards.without, handed in), which YIELDS for a frame or more, and
	no frame may show ground that is intact but not drawn. So until the new copy is there the last one
	stays, and when a wound has closed the skin itself is shown again beside it: grass may lie over an
	open wound for those frames, never a hole over whole ground.

	The skin is LIVE user content, written only by Reactor/Display's hide and show. The copies are not
	saved (Archivable off, under the runtime's folder, marked _PartIcleEmit) and nothing collides with them.

	  SkinDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without) -> skins
	  skins.draw(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
	    ground: a stacked ground; layer: its skin's layer; rectangles: the intact rest of the ground's
	    face `face` (Reactor/Ground), or nil: the skin is whole again.
	  skins.clear()   every skin whole again
	  SkinDisplay.holes(size, rectangles, face) -> { { minU, minV, maxU, maxV }, ... }
	    What of the face of a box of that size the rectangles leave open. Maths only.
]]

local Display = require(script.Parent.Display)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

-- Two edges this near are one.
local SAME = 0.01
-- A cutter reaches this far past the ground along the struck face's axis, to both sides.
local THROUGH = 4

local SkinDisplay = {}

local function edgesOf(low, high, rectangles, fromKey, toKey)
	local edges = { low, high }
	for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
		table.insert(edges, math.clamp(rectangle[fromKey], low, high))
		table.insert(edges, math.clamp(rectangle[toKey], low, high))
	end
	table.sort(edges)
	local distinct = { edges[1] }
	for position = 2, #edges do
		if edges[position] - distinct[#distinct] > SAME then
			table.insert(distinct, edges[position])
		end
	end
	return distinct
end

function SkinDisplay.holes(size, rectangles, face)
	local uAxis, vAxis = Sites.faceAxes(face.axis)
	local us = edgesOf(-size[uAxis] / 2, size[uAxis] / 2, rectangles, "minU", "maxU")
	local vs = edgesOf(-size[vAxis] / 2, size[vAxis] / 2, rectangles, "minV", "maxV")
	local holes = {}
	for row = 1, #vs - 1 do
		local v = (vs[row] + vs[row + 1]) / 2
		-- Open cells of a row side by side are one hole.
		local run = nil
		for column = 1, #us - 1 do
			local u = (us[column] + us[column + 1]) / 2
			local covered = false
			for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
				if u > rectangle.minU and u < rectangle.maxU and v > rectangle.minV and v < rectangle.maxV then
					covered = true
					break
				end
			end
			if covered then
				run = nil
			elseif run then
				run.maxU = us[column + 1]
			else
				run = { minU = us[column], minV = vs[row], maxU = us[column + 1], maxV = vs[row + 1] }
				table.insert(holes, run)
			end
		end
	end
	return holes
end

-- Whether every hole of `before` is still open in `now`.
local function stillOpen(before, now)
	for _, hole in ipairs(before) do
		local u = (hole.minU + hole.maxU) / 2
		local v = (hole.minV + hole.maxV) / 2
		local open = false
		for _, other in ipairs(now) do
			-- A hole's middle may lie on the line between two new ones.
			if u >= other.minU and u <= other.maxU and v >= other.minV and v <= other.maxV then
				open = true
				break
			end
		end
		if not open then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

function SkinDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without)
	-- part -> { copy, kept (what Display.show puts back), holes, version }
	local drawn = {}
	local skins = {}

	local function whole(part)
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			return
		end
		drawn[part] = nil
		if state.copy then
			state.copy:Destroy()
		end
		if state.kept then
			Display.show(part, onServer, state.kept)
		end
	end

	-- The engine's copy as what is drawn of the skin.
	local function dress(copy, part)
		copy.Name = "SkinRest"
		copy.Archivable = false
		copy.Anchored = true
		copy.CanCollide = false
		copy.CanQuery = false
		copy.CanTouch = false
		copy.Locked = true
		if copy:IsA("PartOperation") and part:IsA("PartOperation") then
			copy.UsePartColor = part.UsePartColor
		end
		-- On a server the skin is hidden through its own Transparency, which the copy took.
		copy.Transparency = Display.ownTransparency(part)
		Index.unmark(copy)
		copy:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	end

	function skins.draw(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
		local part = layer.part
		local holes = rectangles and SkinDisplay.holes(ground.size, rectangles, face) or {}
		if #holes == 0 then
			whole(part)
			return
		end
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			state = { copy = nil, kept = nil, holes = {}, version = 0 }
			drawn[part] = state
		end
		-- A wound has closed: the skin covers its place until the new copy is there.
		if state.kept and not stillOpen(state.holes, holes) then
			Display.show(part, onServer, state.kept)
			state.kept = nil
		end
		state.holes = holes
		state.version += 1
		local version = state.version
		local boxes = table.create(#holes)
		local through = ground.size[face.axis] + 2 * THROUGH
		for position, hole in ipairs(holes) do
			local centre = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, (hole.minU + hole.maxU) / 2, (hole.minV + hole.maxV) / 2, 0)
			boxes[position] = {
				frame = ground.frame * CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z),
				size = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, hole.maxU - hole.minU, hole.maxV - hole.minV, through),
			}
		end
		task.spawn(function()
			local copy = without(part, boxes)
			if drawn[part] ~= state or state.version ~= version then
				if copy then
					copy:Destroy()
				end
				return
			end
			-- The engine gave nothing: what is drawn stays.
			if not copy then
				return
			end
			dress(copy, part)
			copy.Parent = folder
			if state.copy then
				state.copy:Destroy()
			end
			state.copy = copy
			-- Hidden last, so the copy is there in the frame the skin goes.
			if not state.kept then
				state.kept = Display.hide(part, onServer, true)
			end
		end)
	end

	function skins.clear()
		for part in pairs(table.clone(drawn)) do
			whole(part)
		end
	end

	return skins
end

return SkinDisplay

--[[
	Slash: what the sides of a cut do. Part of Reactor/Play: the functions take a play and read and
	write its own tables. Maths on Vector3 and CFrame values, no instances.

	A Linear Force with a Cut (record.cut = { mode, pushAlong, pushApart }) carves the parts its blade
	touches (Reactor/Carve). A carved piece carries piece.slash = { origin, normal, heading, kerf, by }
	(one table per part, `by` the Force it was cut for) and piece.side (1 or -1) or piece.bit (debris).

	The first time that Force reaches the play its cuts show and their sides are let go:
	  - The upper side of a sloping cut is loose. With no Push Apart it drops onto the cut and slides
	    down it, then falls (Rocks/Trajectory.slide); Push Along sends it along the Force's heading.
	    A level cut with no push only closes. With a Push Apart it is thrown clear at once.
	  - The lower side is carried; Reactor/Support lets it fall when nothing carries it.
	  - Of an upright cut both sides stand unless a push throws each to its own side.
	  - A lone side (the blade ended inside the part) stands.
	Pushes are distances, as a Force's Strength is (Force/Fields.throwSpeed). Bits are thrown by the
	Force's Strength as its front reaches them, whatever the Reactor's Hold.

	A standing side is kept like a piece of cracked ground: RESTING with play.crackFrame[index] at its
	pose. Pieces of a piece cut again (Reactor/Recarve) stand where that piece stood, so everything
	here goes by where a side stands now. A slide stops where one ray along it meets the world.

	Slash.kick(play, record, kicked)
	  Called by Play:_applyImpulse for every Impulse; the sides and bits it lets go join `kicked`.
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)
local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- A push under this many studs is no push.
local LEAST_PUSH = 0.05
-- A fresh cut's loose side slides on any slope steeper than about 5 degrees.
local SLIDE_FRICTION = 0.08
-- An acceleration under this (studs/s^2) is no slide.
local LEAST_SLIDE = 1
-- Longest slide, seconds.
local MOST_SLIDE = 4
-- Share of its tumble a side takes over the edge.
local TIP_SHARE = 0.5
-- A bit strays sideways by up to this share of its speed.
local BIT_STRAY = 0.35
-- Halvings that find when a slide has gone a given way.
local TIME_STEPS = 16

local Slash = {}

-- Where a side stands: its rest pose unless the piece it was cut from stood out of place.
local function stoodAt(play, index)
	return play.crackFrame[index] or play.pieces[index].rest
end

-- How far a box of half-lengths `half` at `stood` reaches along a unit direction.
local function reachAlong(stood, half, direction)
	return math.abs(stood.XVector:Dot(direction)) * half.X + math.abs(stood.YVector:Dot(direction)) * half.Y + math.abs(stood.ZVector:Dot(direction)) * half.Z
end

-- How far the pieces reach past their common middle along a direction: the way the middle must go
-- before it is over the edge.
local function overhang(play, indices, direction)
	local total = 0
	local farthest = -math.huge
	for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
		local stood = stoodAt(play, index)
		local along = stood.Position:Dot(direction)
		total += along
		farthest = math.max(farthest, along + reachAlong(stood, play.pieces[index].halfExt, direction))
	end
	return farthest - total / #indices
end

-- Where a slide is `time` seconds in.
local function slid(velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, time)
	local settled = math.min(time / settleTime, 1)
	return velocity * time + acceleration * (0.5 * time * time) + settle * (settled * settled)
end

-- Seconds a piece may slide before the world is in its way (`duration` at most): one ray along the
-- slide finds the surface, and the piece slides until its box touches that plane.
local function clearFor(play, index, velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, duration)
	local stood = stoodAt(play, index)
	local half = play.pieces[index].halfExt
	local start = stood.Position
	local travel = slid(velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, duration)
	local distance = travel.Magnitude
	if distance < TINY then
		return duration
	end
	local direction = travel / distance
	local hit = play.castRay(start, direction * (distance + reachAlong(stood, half, direction)))
	if not hit then
		return duration
	end
	local normal = hit.Normal
	local seat = hit.Position:Dot(normal) + reachAlong(stood, half, normal)
	local function clear(time)
		return (start + slid(velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, time)):Dot(normal) >= seat
	end
	if clear(duration) then
		return duration
	end
	local low, high = 0, duration
	for _ = 1, TIME_STEPS do
		local middle = (low + high) / 2
		if clear(middle) then
			low = middle
		else
			high = middle
		end
	end
	return low
end

-- Puts a standing carved piece on a path of its own.
local function launch(play, index, path, built)
	play.display.wake(index)
	play.awake += 1
	play.hidden += 1
	play.path[index] = path
	play.pathStart[index] = play.clock
	play.pathBuilt[index] = built
	play.lastFrame[index] = stoodAt(play, index)
	if not built then
		table.insert(play.buildQueue, index)
	end
	play.state[index] = FLYING
	table.insert(play.flying, index)
	play.supportStale = true
end

-- The loose side of a sloping cut with no Push Apart; `along` is its Push Along speed. All its
-- pieces take one slide so the side leaves as one.
local function slideOff(play, indices, slash, downhill, sine, cosine, along)
	local gravity = play:_rolled(indices[1])
	local accel = gravity * (sine - SLIDE_FRICTION * cosine)
	-- It falls onto the cut first: the kerf, straight down.
	local drop = slash.kerf / math.max(cosine, TINY)
	local settle = UP * -drop
	local settleTime = math.sqrt(2 * drop / math.max(gravity, TINY))
	local slides = downhill ~= nil and accel > LEAST_SLIDE
	if not slides and along <= 0 then
		for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
			play:_rolled(index)
			local stood = stoodAt(play, index)
			local lead = Trajectory.slide(stood.Position, ZERO, stood.Rotation, ZERO, settleTime, settle, settleTime)
			launch(play, index, Trajectory.settled(lead, UP), true)
		end
		return
	end

	local velocity = slash.heading * along
	local acceleration = ZERO
	local duration = MOST_SLIDE
	if slides then
		acceleration = downhill * accel
		local length = overhang(play, indices, downhill)
		local start = velocity:Dot(downhill)
		duration = math.min(duration, (-start + math.sqrt(start * start + 2 * accel * length)) / accel)
	end
	if along > 0 then
		duration = math.min(duration, overhang(play, indices, slash.heading) / along)
	end
	for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
		play:_rolled(index)
		local stood = stoodAt(play, index)
		local own = clearFor(play, index, velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, duration)
		local lead = Trajectory.slide(stood.Position, velocity, stood.Rotation, acceleration, own, settle, settleTime)
		local finish = stood.Position + slid(velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, own)
		local leave = velocity + acceleration * own
		-- Over the edge it tips about the level axis across its way out.
		local level = Vector3.new(leave.X, 0, leave.Z)
		local spin = ZERO
		if level.Magnitude > TINY then
			spin = UP:Cross(level.Unit) * (play.settings.rollTumble() * TIP_SHARE)
		end
		launch(play, index, Trajectory.led(lead, Trajectory.ballistic(finish, leave, stood.Rotation, spin)), false)
	end
end

-- Lets go of the sides of one part's cut. group = { slash, sides = { [1], [-1] }, first }.
local function release(play, group, cut)
	local slash = group.slash
	local sides = group.sides
	-- The blade ended inside the part: it is in one piece, nothing is let go.
	if #sides[1] == 0 or #sides[-1] == 0 then
		return
	end
	local gravity = play:_rolled(group.first)
	local along = 0
	if cut.pushAlong > LEAST_PUSH then
		along = Fields.throwSpeed(cut.pushAlong, gravity)
	end
	local apart = 0
	if cut.pushApart > LEAST_PUSH then
		apart = Fields.throwSpeed(cut.pushApart, gravity)
	end
	local over, downhill, sine, cosine = Blade.slope(slash)
	if over == 0 then
		if along > 0 or apart > 0 then
			for side = -1, 1, 2 do
				for _, index in ipairs(sides[side]) do
					play:_push(index, slash.heading * along + slash.normal * (side * apart))
				end
			end
		end
		return
	end
	local loose = sides[over]
	if apart > 0 then
		for _, index in ipairs(loose) do
			play:_push(index, slash.heading * along + slash.normal * (over * apart))
		end
		return
	end
	slideOff(play, loose, slash, downhill, sine, cosine, along)
end

-- Sides that lie where their piece fell or fly as it flew: a push throws each to its own side.
local function throwLoose(play, record, kicked)
	local cut = record.cut
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		local slash = piece.slash
		local state = play.state[index]
		if slash and slash.by == record and piece.side and (state == LANDED or state == FLYING) and not kicked[index] then
			kicked[index] = true
			local gravity = play:_rolled(index)
			local push = ZERO
			if cut.pushAlong > LEAST_PUSH then
				push += slash.heading * Fields.throwSpeed(cut.pushAlong, gravity)
			end
			if cut.pushApart > LEAST_PUSH then
				push += slash.normal * (piece.side * Fields.throwSpeed(cut.pushApart, gravity))
			end
			if push.Magnitude > TINY then
				play:_push(index, push)
				play:_takeTime(record)
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Shows every part this Force cut and lets its sides go.
local function letGo(play, record, kicked)
	throwLoose(play, record, kicked)
	local groups = {}
	local ordered = {}
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		local slash = piece.slash
		if slash and slash.by == record and play.state[index] == RESTING and not play.pendingPush[index] then
			local group = groups[slash]
			if not group then
				group = { slash = slash, sides = { [1] = {}, [-1] = {} }, first = index }
				groups[slash] = group
				table.insert(ordered, group)
			end
			if piece.side then
				play.crackFrame[index] = stoodAt(play, index)
				kicked[index] = true
				-- A fixed side stands whatever the cut (a part with a slot, a ground's patch).
				if not piece.fixed then
					table.insert(group.sides[piece.side], index)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	for _, group in ipairs(ordered) do
		play.display.wake(group.first)
		play.hidden += 1
		release(play, group, record.cut)
	end
	if #ordered > 0 then
		play:_takeTime(record)
	end
end

-- The bits the Force's front has reached go, along its heading.
local function throwBits(play, record, kicked)
	local field = record.field
	local strength = record.strength
	local heading = Fields.heading(field, strength < 0)
	local origin = field.origin.Position
	local axis = field.origin.LookVector
	local random = play.settings.random
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		local slash = piece.slash
		local state = play.state[index]
		if piece.bit and slash.by == record and not kicked[index] and (state == RESTING or state == LANDED or state == FLYING) and not play.pendingPush[index] then
			local distance = math.clamp((play:_position(index) - origin):Dot(axis), field.inner, field.range)
			if distance <= record.front then
				kicked[index] = true
				local spread = 1 + record.variation * (random() * 2 - 1)
				local throw = strength * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance / field.range) * spread
				local speed = Fields.throwSpeed(throw, play:_rolled(index))
				local stray = slash.normal * ((random() * 2 - 1) * BIT_STRAY * speed)
				play:_push(index, heading * speed + stray)
			end
		end
	end
end

function Slash.kick(play, record, kicked)
	if not record.cut then
		return
	end
	local shown = play.slashed
	if not shown then
		shown = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
		play.slashed = shown
	end
	if not shown[record] then
		shown[record] = true
		letGo(play, record, kicked)
	end
	throwBits(play, record, kicked)
end

return Slash

--[[
	Support: which pieces of a Reactor hold each other up, so a piece left with nothing under or beside
	it can fall. Numbers only, no instances.

	Two pieces are neighbours when their boxes meet face to face: world-axis boxes around each piece at
	rest, no farther apart than a small margin along one axis and overlapping by a good part of the
	smaller box along the other two. Boxes meeting only at an edge or corner do not hold each other. The
	two sides of a blade's cut hold each other across its kerf (piece.slash, Reactor/Carve). A piece is
	anchored when the caller says so (Reactor/init: something that is not the Reactor lies right under
	it). A piece is supported when a chain of standing neighbours leads from it to a standing anchored piece.

	  Support.build(pieces, isAnchored) -> graph; graph.supported[index] is true for every piece
	    supported while everything stands. A piece that floats from the start is not, and never falls.
	  Support.unsupported(graph, isStanding) -> the pieces that were supported at rest, still stand,
	    and have lost their last chain to an anchor.
]]

local Support = {}

-- How far apart two boxes may be and still touch, in studs.
local TOUCH_MARGIN = 0.15
-- Along the two axes of a shared face, the boxes must overlap by this share of the smaller one.
local FACE_SHARE = 0.25
-- Grid cell size the boxes are sorted into, so only nearby pieces are compared.
local LEAST_CELL = 2

-- Half the size of the world-axis box around a piece at rest.
function Support.worldHalf(piece)
	local rest = piece.rest
	local half = piece.halfExt
	local right, up, back = rest.XVector, rest.YVector, rest.ZVector
	return Vector3.new(
		math.abs(right.X) * half.X + math.abs(up.X) * half.Y + math.abs(back.X) * half.Z,
		math.abs(right.Y) * half.X + math.abs(up.Y) * half.Y + math.abs(back.Y) * half.Z,
		math.abs(right.Z) * half.X + math.abs(up.Z) * half.Y + math.abs(back.Z) * half.Z
	)
end

-- Along one axis: 2 when the boxes overlap deeply enough to share a face, 1 when they touch, 0 when apart.
local function contact(offset, firstHalf, secondHalf)
	local overlap = firstHalf + secondHalf - math.abs(offset)
	if overlap >= FACE_SHARE * 2 * math.min(firstHalf, secondHalf) then
		return 2
	elseif overlap >= -TOUCH_MARGIN then
		return 1
	end
	return 0
end

-- Face to face: touching along every axis and overlapping deeply along at least two.
function Support.touching(firstCentre, firstHalf, secondCentre, secondHalf)
	local alongX = contact(firstCentre.X - secondCentre.X, firstHalf.X, secondHalf.X)
	local alongY = contact(firstCentre.Y - secondCentre.Y, firstHalf.Y, secondHalf.Y)
	local alongZ = contact(firstCentre.Z - secondCentre.Z, firstHalf.Z, secondHalf.Z)
	if alongX == 0 or alongY == 0 or alongZ == 0 then
		return false
	end
	return alongX + alongY + alongZ >= 5
end

-- Every piece reachable from the standing anchored ones through standing neighbours.
local function reached(graph, isStanding)
	local seen = {}
	local queue = {}
	for index in pairs(graph.anchored) do
		if isStanding(index) then
			seen[index] = true
			table.insert(queue, index)
		end
	end
	local head = 1
	while head <= #queue do
		local index = queue[head]
		head += 1
		for _, neighbour in ipairs(graph.neighbours[index]) do
			if not seen[neighbour] and isStanding(neighbour) then
				seen[neighbour] = true
				table.insert(queue, neighbour)
			end
		end
	end
	return seen
end

function Support.build(pieces, isAnchored)
	local count = #pieces
	local centres = table.create(count)
	local halves = table.create(count)
	local cell = LEAST_CELL
	for index, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		centres[index] = piece.rest.Position
		local half = Support.worldHalf(piece)
		-- The sides of a blade's cut stand a kerf apart and still hold each other: each box reaches half the kerf.
		local slash = piece.slash
		if slash then
			local normal = slash.normal
			half += Vector3.new(math.abs(normal.X), math.abs(normal.Y), math.abs(normal.Z)) * (slash.kerf / 2)
		end
		halves[index] = half
		cell = math.max(cell, half.X * 2, half.Y * 2, half.Z * 2)
	end

	-- A box is listed in every cell it reaches; two boxes are compared once, in the first cell they share.
	local cells = {}
	local neighbours = table.create(count)
	local paired = {}
	for index = 1, count do
		neighbours[index] = {}
		local centre, half = centres[index], halves[index]
		for x = math.floor((centre.X - half.X - TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell), math.floor((centre.X + half.X + TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell) do
			for y = math.floor((centre.Y - half.Y - TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell), math.floor((centre.Y + half.Y + TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell) do
				for z = math.floor((centre.Z - half.Z - TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell), math.floor((centre.Z + half.Z + TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell) do
					local key = x .. "," .. y .. "," .. z
					local members = cells[key]
					if not members then
						members = {}
						cells[key] = members
					end
					for _, other in ipairs(members) do
						local pair = other * (count + 1) + index
						if not paired[pair] then
							paired[pair] = true
							if Support.touching(centre, half, centres[other], halves[other]) then
								table.insert(neighbours[index], other)
								table.insert(neighbours[other], index)
							end
						end
					end
					table.insert(members, index)
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local anchored = {}
	for index = 1, count do
		if isAnchored(index) then
			anchored[index] = true
		end
	end
	local graph = { neighbours = neighbours, anchored = anchored, supported = {} }
	graph.supported = reached(graph, function()
		return true
	end)
	return graph
end

function Support.unsupported(graph, isStanding)
	local held = reached(graph, isStanding)
	local fallen = {}
	for index in pairs(graph.supported) do
		if not held[index] and isStanding(index) then
			table.insert(fallen, index)
		end
	end
	table.sort(fallen)
	return fallen
end

return Support

--[[
	WoundBudget: what a Reactor's wounds hold against its Max Pieces (Reactor/Wounds mixes these methods
	in; `self` is the wounds). Logic only.

	The budget covers every wound of the Reactor's grounds: the pieces of groups that stay plus those a
	wound still being cut is expected to bring. A crack that would pass it first sweeps away blade debris
	(oldest wounds first; a gash stays, its bits are litter), then sends the oldest groups back early, but
	only while that can help: if the groups that must stay are over the budget by themselves, no other
	group is healed for nothing.

	WoundBudget.livePieces(wound) -> the pieces of a wound that count: all but those cut again
	WoundBudget.methods = { _held, _sweep, _send, _makeRoom, _room }
	  _held() -> the pieces the budget counts
	  _sweep(extra)               removes landed debris until `extra` more pieces would fit
	  _send(group, after, time)   every wound of a group starts on its way back
	  _makeRoom(extra, spare)     brings what is held, and `extra` more, under the budget
	  _room(wound)                what a later crack may add to a wound
]]

local Recut = require(script.Parent.Recut)

local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3

local WoundBudget = {}
local methods = {}
WoundBudget.methods = methods

-- The pieces of a wound that count: all but those a later crack cut again.
function WoundBudget.livePieces(wound)
	local pieces = 0
	for _, piece in ipairs(wound.play.pieces) do
		if not piece.retired then
			pieces += 1
		end
	end
	return pieces
end

local livePieces = WoundBudget.livePieces

-- The pieces of groups that stay, plus those a wound still being cut is expected to bring.
function methods:_held()
	local pieces = 0
	for _, wound in ipairs(self.open) do
		if not wound.group.leaving then
			if wound.play then
				pieces += livePieces(wound)
			else
				pieces += wound.expected
			end
		end
	end
	return pieces
end

-- Every wound of a group starts back now: `after` in `time` seconds, or in the play's own After Time when nil.
function methods:_send(group, after, time)
	group.sent = true
	for _, wound in ipairs(group.wounds) do
		local play = wound.play
		if play and play.phase == "live" then
			play.settings.After = after
			play.settings.AfterDelay = 0
			if time then
				play.settings.AfterTime = time
			end
		end
	end
end

local function beingCut(group)
	for _, wound in ipairs(group.wounds) do
		if not wound.play then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- Landed blade debris is litter: the oldest wounds' is removed until `extra` more pieces fit. A swept
-- bit is retired for good, so a closing wound does not bring it back.
function methods:_sweep(extra)
	local over = self:_held() + extra - self.maxPieces
	for _, wound in ipairs(self.open) do
		local play = wound.play
		if play and play.phase == "live" then
			for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
				if over <= 0 then
					return
				end
				if piece.bit and not piece.retired and play.state[index] == LANDED then
					piece.retired = true
					play.state[index] = GONE
					play.display.drop(index)
					play.awake -= 1
					over -= 1
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

-- The pieces that cannot be sent back now: those of `spare` and of every group with a wound still being cut.
local function staying(self, spare)
	local pieces = 0
	for _, group in ipairs(self.groups) do
		if not group.leaving and (group == spare or beingCut(group)) then
			for _, wound in ipairs(group.wounds) do
				if wound.play then
					pieces += livePieces(wound)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return pieces
end

-- Brings what is held, and `extra` more, under the budget by sending the oldest groups back. Never a
-- group with a wound still being cut, nor `spare` (the group a later crack is about to break again);
-- none at all when those are over the budget by themselves.
function methods:_makeRoom(extra, spare)
	self:_sweep(extra)
	if staying(self, spare) + extra > self.maxPieces then
		return
	end
	local position = 1
	while position <= #self.groups and self:_held() + extra > self.maxPieces do
		local group = self.groups[position]
		if group == spare or group.leaving or beingCut(group) then
			position += 1
		else
			self:_leave(group)
			if self.groups[position] == group then
				position += 1
			end
		end
	end
end

-- What a later crack may add to a wound: its play is held to the room all the wounds leave.
function methods:_room(wound)
	local settings = wound.play.settings
	local live = livePieces(wound)
	local held = self:_held()
	settings.MaxPieces = live + math.max(self.maxPieces - held, 0)
	settings.MostPieces = live + math.max(self.maxPieces * Recut.PLATE_ROOM - held, 0)
end

return WoundBudget

--[[
	Wounds  -  the cracks of a Reactor's ground parts. Logic only (instances, the engine's cut and the
	plays come through Wounds.new), so it runs under the luau CLI.
	A ground (a block part, Break "Shards", pattern "Cracks") is never cut whole. An Impulse opens a
	wound: a square of the struck face around the hit (a strip along a Linear Force's split,
	Reactor/Footprint), less what open wounds hold; each rectangle is cut from its own template
	(Reactor/Patches) and its pieces are one Reactor/Play. A Cut carves a gash under its blade, through
	the ground; over an open wound it cuts what stands again (Reactor/Recarve). The rest of the ground
	is drawn as boxes around the wounds (Reactor/GroundDisplay).
	Wounds that touch are one group and heal together, after the group's Delay counted from when its
	last piece came to rest (After and Delay: the Reactor's, or the last Force's record.after).
	The cut takes a few frames: a wound holds its ground at once and shows when its pieces arrive;
	the Force kicks late (Play:strike).
	  Wounds.new(options) -> wounds. options: grounds { { part, frame, size } }, pieceCount,
	    maxPieces (over all grounds; older groups return early to make room, Reactor/WoundBudget),
	    after, afterDelay, snap, cut(jobs, done), play(pieces, record) -> play, display,
	    draw(ground, rectangles, face), isCurrent(), revive()
	  wounds:watch(record), wounds:strike(record) (again only once the Force moved half its Range)
	  wounds:step(dt, override, frozen) -> "active" | "dormant" | "done"
	  wounds:restore(), wounds:busy(), wounds:count() -> open wounds, live pieces
]]

local Ground = require(script.Parent.Ground)
local Footprint = require(script.Parent.Footprint)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)
local Recrack = require(script.Parent.Recrack)
local Recarve = require(script.Parent.Recarve)
local WoundBudget = require(script.Parent.WoundBudget)
local Recut = require(script.Parent.Recut)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)
local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Registry = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Registry)

-- A wound follows a Force within this many times its square's half-diagonal (its debris lies there).
local WATCH_REACH = 1.5
-- A Force that travels cracks again once it has moved this share of its Range.
local STRIKE_AGAIN = 0.5
-- The seconds a wound takes to return when it makes room for a new one.
local QUICK_RETURN = 0.25

local Wounds = {}
Wounds.__index = Wounds
Wounds.PATCH_REACH = Footprint.PATCH_REACH
-- _held, _send, _makeRoom and _room: what the wounds hold against Max Pieces.
for name, method in pairs(WoundBudget.methods) do
	Wounds[name] = method
end
local livePieces = WoundBudget.livePieces

function Wounds.new(options)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Wounds)
	self.grounds = options.grounds
	self.pieceCount = options.pieceCount
	self.maxPieces = options.maxPieces
	self.after = options.after
	self.afterDelay = options.afterDelay
	self.snap = options.snap
	self.cut = options.cut
	self.play = options.play
	self.draw = options.draw
	self.isCurrent = options.isCurrent
	self.revive = options.revive
	-- Every wound that holds ground, oldest first; one being cut has no play yet.
	self.open = {}
	-- The groups of wounds that touch, oldest first: { wounds, idle, after, delay, sent, leaving }.
	self.groups = {}
	-- record -> where it last cracked; a record that is over is forgotten with it.
	self.struck = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
	return self
end

-- A ground with nothing held is free to crack on any face again.
local function settle(ground)
	if ground.sheet and ground.sheet:isWhole() then
		ground.sheet = nil
		ground.face = nil
	end
end

-- Sends a group back early, all of it, so none of its cracks is left cut off. A wound with
-- pieces in the air cannot return yet: it goes at once.
function Wounds:_leave(group)
	group.leaving = true
	for _, wound in ipairs(table.clone(group.wounds)) do
		local play = wound.play
		if play.phase == "live" and (#play.flying > 0 or #play.driven > 0 or #play.pendingWake > 0) then
			self:_close(wound)
			settle(wound.ground)
		end
	end
	self:_send(group, "Return", QUICK_RETURN)
end

-- What of a ground is drawn as intact: all of it but the wounds that show.
function Wounds:_draw(ground)
	local sheet = ground.sheet
	local unshown = {}
	local shown = false
	for _, wound in ipairs(self.open) do
		if wound.ground == ground then
			if wound.shown then
				shown = true
			else
				unshown[wound] = true
			end
		end
	end
	if not sheet or not shown then
		self.draw(ground, nil, nil)
	else
		self.draw(ground, sheet:remainder(unshown), ground.face)
	end
end

function Wounds:_close(wound, quiet)
	if wound.closed then
		return
	end
	wound.closed = true
	table.remove(self.open, table.find(self.open, wound))
	table.clear(wound.cracks)
	local group = wound.group
	table.remove(group.wounds, table.find(group.wounds, wound))
	if #group.wounds == 0 then
		table.remove(self.groups, table.find(self.groups, group))
	end
	-- The play is thrown away with its wound: only what it shows has to go.
	if wound.display then
		wound.display.clear()
	end
	local ground = wound.ground
	if ground.sheet then
		ground.sheet:release(wound)
	end
	if not quiet then
		self:_draw(ground)
	end
end

-- A crack touched the group: its wait starts again, on the word of the last Force to crack it
-- (record.after) or the Reactor's. One leaving keeps leaving.
local function touch(group, record)
	group.idle = 0
	if record.after and not group.leaving then
		group.after = record.after
		group.delay = record.afterDelay
	end
end

-- The ground keeps its face and its sheet: whoever closes a group is about to claim on it.
function Wounds:_closeGroup(group)
	for _, wound in ipairs(table.clone(group.wounds)) do
		self:_close(wound)
	end
end

-- Two groups a crack touches both become one, the older of them.
function Wounds:_merge(first, second)
	if not first or first == second then
		return second
	end
	local older, newer = first, second
	if table.find(self.groups, second) < table.find(self.groups, first) then
		older, newer = second, first
	end
	for _, wound in ipairs(newer.wounds) do
		wound.group = older
		table.insert(older.wounds, wound)
	end
	table.remove(self.groups, table.find(self.groups, newer))
	return older
end

-- A wound that is open and still its Reactor's: what Reactor/Recrack asks before it answers.
local function stillOpen(self, wound)
	return function()
		return not wound.closed and self.isCurrent()
	end
end

-- A later Force on a showing wound: a blade cuts again (Reactor/Recarve), an Impulse cracks again
-- (Reactor/Recrack).
function Wounds:_again(wound, record, kicked)
	touch(wound.group, record)
	self:_room(wound)
	local again = if record.cut then Recarve else Recrack
	again.request(wound, record, kicked, stillOpen(self, wound), self.revive)
end

-- A later Impulse on an open wound; one still being cut keeps the record until its pieces arrive.
function Wounds:_crackAgain(wound, record)
	local play = wound.play
	if not play then
		table.insert(wound.waiting, record)
		return
	end
	if play:watch(record) then
		-- A later crack adds pieces, older groups making room as for a new wound (Reactor/Recut). A blade's
		-- cut is made whatever the room, its debris only while there is some.
		if record.cut then
			self:_sweep(Footprint.bladePieces(record.cut.mode))
		else
			self:_makeRoom((record.pieces or self.pieceCount) * Sites.LAYERS, wound.group)
		end
		self:_again(wound, record, play.kicks[record])
	end
end

-- The pieces of a wound are there: it shows, and the Forces that wait for it strike.
function Wounds:_show(wound, jobs, sets)
	if wound.closed or not self.isCurrent() then
		return
	end
	local ground = wound.ground
	local pieces = {}
	local siblings = {}
	for position, job in ipairs(jobs) do
		local shards = sets[position]
		if shards and (#shards >= 2 or shards.slash) then
			Pieces.ofSet(pieces, ground.part, job.frame, shards, siblings, { size = job.size, face = job.face }, ground.layers)
		else
			-- No cut came: the rectangle stands in whole and never moves (a block per layer when stacked).
			local blocks = job.layers or { { offset = Vector3.zero, size = job.size } }
			for _, share in ipairs(blocks) do
				local part = ground.part
				if share.index then
					part = ground.layers[share.index].part
				end
				local piece = Pieces.ofBlock(part, job.frame * CFrame.new(share.offset), share.size)
				piece.fixed = true
				piece.siblings = siblings
				table.insert(pieces, piece)
				table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
			end
		end
	end
	-- The strikes are this Force's: Reactor/Crack tells by that which pieces its split reaches.
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		if piece.strike then
			piece.strike.by = wound.record
		end
		if piece.slash then
			piece.slash.by = wound.record
		end
	end
	local play, display = self.play(pieces, wound.record)
	wound.play = play
	wound.display = display
	wound.shown = true
	-- When a wound goes back is its group's to say (step, below).
	play.settings.After = "Stay"
	touch(wound.group, wound.record)
	-- Waking one piece stands the whole wound in, at rest (Reactor/Display: siblings).
	display.wake(1)
	self:_draw(ground)

	play:strike(wound.record)
	for _, record in ipairs(wound.waiting) do
		local struck, kicked = play:strike(record)
		if struck then
			self:_again(wound, record, kicked)
		end
	end
	table.clear(wound.waiting)
	self.revive()
end

-- One ground under one Impulse.
function Wounds:_crack(ground, record, hit, reach)
	local size = ground.size
	local hitInPart = ground.frame:PointToObjectSpace(hit)
	-- A Force farther from the ground than its Range moves none of it.
	if (hitInPart - Sites.hitIn(size, hitInPart)).Magnitude > reach then
		return
	end
	local axis, side = Sites.face(size, hitInPart)
	local face = ground.face
	if record.cut then
		-- A blade goes through whichever side its Force stands on: the open face, or the + side of the nearest.
		side = 1
		if face then
			axis, side = face.axis, face.side
		end
	end
	if face and (face.axis ~= axis or face.side ~= side) then
		-- A ground cracks on one face for as long as a wound of it is open.
		return
	end
	if not face then
		ground.face = { axis = axis, side = side }
		ground.uAxis, ground.vAxis = Sites.faceAxes(axis)
		ground.sheet = Ground.new(size[ground.uAxis] / 2, size[ground.vAxis] / 2, self.snap)
	end
	local sheet = ground.sheet
	local seed = Sites.seedAt(hit)
	local footprint
	if record.cut then
		self:_sweep(2 * Footprint.bladePieces(record.cut.mode))
		footprint = Footprint.ofBlade(ground, Blade.of(record.field, record.cut), record.cut.mode, self.maxPieces - self:_held())
		if not footprint then
			settle(ground)
			return
		end
	else
		footprint = Footprint.of(ground, record.field, hitInPart, reach, seed)
	end

	-- The wounds this area touches join its group; a group on its way back closes at once.
	local touched = sheet:touching(footprint.minU, footprint.minV, footprint.maxU, footprint.maxV)
	local group = nil
	for _, wound in ipairs(touched) do
		if not wound.closed then
			if wound.group.sent then
				self:_closeGroup(wound.group)
			else
				group = self:_merge(group, wound.group)
			end
		end
	end
	for _, wound in ipairs(touched) do
		if not wound.closed then
			self:_crackAgain(wound, record)
		end
	end

	-- A Force whose shape touches none of the ground opens nothing (a Vortex over it reaches up).
	if footprint.probes and not Fields.reachesAny(record.field, ground.frame, footprint.probes, record.strength < 0) then
		settle(ground)
		return
	end
	local pieces = record.pieces or self.pieceCount
	local wound = { ground = ground, record = record, cracks = {}, waiting = {}, pieceCount = self.pieceCount }
	local rectangles = sheet:claimArea(wound, footprint.minU, footprint.minV, footprint.maxU, footprint.maxV)
	-- Ground the Force cannot reach is not opened.
	local inReach = false
	for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
		if Footprint.reaches(footprint, rectangle) then
			inReach = true
		end
	end
	if not inReach then
		sheet:release(wound)
		settle(ground)
		return
	end
	local middleU = (footprint.minU + footprint.maxU) / 2
	local middleV = (footprint.minV + footprint.maxV) / 2
	wound.centre = ground.frame:PointToWorldSpace(Sites.alongFace(axis, middleU, middleV, side * size[axis] / 2))
	wound.radius = math.sqrt((footprint.maxU - footprint.minU) ^ 2 + (footprint.maxV - footprint.minV) ^ 2) / 2 * WATCH_REACH
	if not group then
		group = { wounds = {}, idle = 0, after = self.after, delay = self.afterDelay, sent = false, leaving = false }
		table.insert(self.groups, group)
	end
	wound.group = group
	table.insert(group.wounds, wound)
	group.idle = 0
	table.insert(self.open, wound)
	local jobs = {}
	for position, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
		jobs[position] = Footprint.job(ground, rectangle, footprint, hitInPart, seed + position * 7919, #rectangles == 1, pieces)
	end
	wound.expected = Footprint.pieces(footprint, jobs)
	self:_makeRoom(0, nil)
	self.cut(jobs, function(sets)
		self:_show(wound, jobs, sets)
	end)
end

function Wounds:strike(record)
	if record.actsAs ~= "Impulse" then
		return
	end
	local hit = record.field.origin.Position
	local reach = record.field.range
	-- Reactors are told of a Force again whenever it has moved (Force/Registry.announce).
	local last = self.struck[record]
	if last and (last - hit).Magnitude < reach * STRIKE_AGAIN then
		return
	end
	self.struck[record] = hit
	for _, ground in ipairs(self.grounds) do
		self:_crack(ground, record, hit, reach)
	end
end

function Wounds:watch(record)
	local follows = false
	for _, wound in ipairs(self.open) do
		if wound.play and Index.reaches(record.field, wound.centre, wound.radius) and wound.play:watch(record) then
			follows = true
		end
	end
	return follows
end

function Wounds:step(dt, override, frozen)
	local status = "done"
	for _, group in ipairs(self.groups) do
		group.busy = false
	end
	local position = 1
	while position <= #self.open do
		local wound = self.open[position]
		local state = "active"
		if wound.play then
			local timescale = override or Registry.slowest(wound.play.times)
			if frozen then
				timescale = 0
			end
			state = wound.play:step(dt * math.max(timescale, 0))
		end
		if state == "done" then
			self:_close(wound)
			settle(wound.ground)
		else
			position += 1
			-- A wound being cut, or with something moving, holds its group's wait; a live Force does not.
			if not wound.play or wound.play.busy then
				wound.group.busy = true
			end
			if state == "active" then
				status = "active"
			elseif status == "done" then
				status = "dormant"
			end
		end
	end
	-- A group at rest waits its Delay, and then all of it goes back together.
	for _, group in ipairs(self.groups) do
		if group.busy then
			group.idle = 0
		elseif not group.sent and group.after ~= "Stay" then
			status = "active"
			if not frozen then
				group.idle += dt
				if group.idle >= group.delay then
					self:_send(group, group.after, nil)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return status
end

function Wounds:restore()
	for _, wound in ipairs(table.clone(self.open)) do
		self:_close(wound, true)
	end
	self.groups = {}
	for _, ground in ipairs(self.grounds) do
		self.draw(ground, nil, nil)
		ground.sheet = nil
		ground.face = nil
	end
end

-- Whether a wound is being cut: the Reactor must stay at work until its pieces are there.
function Wounds:busy()
	for _, wound in ipairs(self.open) do
		if not wound.play then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function Wounds:count()
	local pieces = 0
	for _, wound in ipairs(self.open) do
		if wound.play then
			pieces += livePieces(wound)
		end
	end
	return #self.open, pieces
end

return Wounds

--[[
	RegisterEmit Mixin  -  Particle:_registerEmit, the universal pData insertion chokepoint.
	Every EmitX type funnels fresh pData through here: cap check, chain-id stamp, ActiveEmits
	insert, OnHit raycast seed, OnEmit fire. Also stamps the per-play "ghost" token
	(emitCtx._playToken) onto pData so AbsoluteEmitAt's PlayHandle can scope Disable /
	SetTimescale / GetParticles to one play, and inherits that play's live timescale window
	onto new emits without writing _tsOverride attributes to the shared source.

	Must be applied (require(script.RegisterEmit)(Particle)) before any emit runs.
]]

local Events = require(script.Parent.Events)
local Pool = require(script.Parent.Pool)
local LinkCF = require(script.Parent.LinkCF)
local NestedEmit = require(script.Parent.NestedEmit)

return function(Particle)

	function Particle:_registerEmit(pData, emitCtx)
		-- Active-particle cap (counts ActiveEmits + linger visuals).
		local cap = self.MAX_ACTIVE_PARTICLES or 1000
		if #self.ActiveEmits + (self._lingerVisualCount or 0) >= cap then
			-- 3D Animate uses LIVE source RT; can't destroy. Clone-Animate (Screen/ImageLabel) destroys.
			local liveRTAnimate = self:_isLiveRTAnimate(pData)
			if pData.IsAnimate and pData._sourceItem then self.ActiveAnimates[pData._sourceItem] = nil end
			-- Emitters create _nestedAlive before registering; flipping it here makes their nested walk a no-op.
			self:_reclaimPData(pData)
			if not liveRTAnimate and pData.VisualPart and pData.VisualPart.Parent then
				-- Cap-reject: route through _releaseOrDestroy so the visual enters the pool.
				self:_releaseOrDestroy(pData, pData.VisualPart)
			end
			return
		end
		-- Root emits with no incoming emitCtx still get a fresh ChainCtx, so OnEmit / OnDeath / OnHit on
		-- one particle share an identity.
		pData.EventChainCtx = (emitCtx and emitCtx.ChainCtx) or pData.EventChainCtx or Events.newChainCtx()

		-- Per-play ghost token: lets PlayHandle sweep / timescale only this play. New emits during an
		-- active play-timescale window inherit it, so the override is never written to the shared source.
		local token = emitCtx and emitCtx._playToken
		if token then
			pData._playToken = token
			if token.TsOverride ~= nil and token.TsUntil and os.clock() < token.TsUntil then
				pData._tsOverride = token.TsOverride
				pData._tsOverrideUntil = token.TsUntil
			end
		end

		-- Play-scoped authoring survives AnimateLoop cycles (EngineReplay re-reads the source).
		if emitCtx then
			pData._playOverrides = emitCtx.Overrides
			pData._playLink = emitCtx._playLink
		end

		-- Link generation: the pool bumps it on every release, so a recycled clone stops being a
		-- valid link for particles that captured it earlier (LinkCF.isValid).
		-- Force/init reads its first link frame only after this has run.
		if pData.Link then pData._linkGen = Pool.linkGen(pData.Link) end
		if emitCtx and emitCtx._parentAlive ~= nil then pData._nestedDriven = true end
		-- A play Emit Into put inside its parent's copy ends with that copy (Engine.step); an
		-- Animate play shows its own live template, never in the copy.
		if pData._parentAlive == nil and not pData.IsAnimate then
			pData._parentAlive = NestedEmit.emitIntoAlive(pData._sourceItem, emitCtx)
		end
		LinkCF.captureEmitFrame(pData)
		table.insert(self.ActiveEmits, pData)
		if pData.Events and pData.Events.OnHit then
			pData.LastHitCheckPos = Events.getWorldPosition(pData)
			pData.HitParams = Events.makeHitParams(pData)
			pData._hitFired = false
		end
		if pData.Events and pData.Events.OnEmit then
			-- Payload built explicitly so EmitIndex (per-burst index) reaches user scripts: Events.fire's nil
			-- fallback cannot see emitCtx.
			local payload = Events.makePayload(self, pData, "OnEmit", emitCtx)
			Events.fire(self, pData, "OnEmit", pData.EventChainCtx, payload)
		end
	end

end

--[[
	Rocks Mixin  -  Emit + Animate + Update for debris bursts.

	Playback is fully predetermined (Rocks/Trajectory.luau): the whole path (arcs, bounces, roll-out,
	rest pose) is computed at emit with about a dozen raycasts per chunk; every frame evaluates
	pose(t) and BulkMoveTo's. Nothing integrates, so Timescale (including reverse) replays the path
	exactly and the game's physics never touches the chunks.

	Path building is spread over frames (TRAJ_BUILD_BUDGET chunks per frame); a chunk flies a
	ballistic placeholder until its path lands.

	OnHit fires from the precomputed first impact (once per burst, or per chunk with HitPerChunk). The
	generic Events.afterUpdate raycast must NOT run here: the Model pivot is the live bounding-box
	center and moves with the chunks. pData._ownsOnHit gates it off (set in Rocks/PDataBuilder;
	checked at the top of Events.afterUpdate).
]]

local GraphMod = require(script.Parent.Graph)
local ContainerFade = require(script.Parent.Container.Fade)
local RangeMod = require(script.Parent.Range)
local Pool = require(script.Parent.Pool)
local EventsMod = require(script.Parent.Events)
local NestedEmit = require(script.Parent.NestedEmit)
local ParticlesMod = require(script.Parent.Particles)
local Trajectory = require(script.Trajectory)
local PDataBuilder = require(script.PDataBuilder)

local MAX_CHUNKS = 32
-- Chunk paths built per frame; each build costs up to ~18 raycasts.
local TRAJ_BUILD_BUDGET = 8
local FAR_CFRAME = CFrame.new(1e9, 1e9, 1e9)
-- Rested chunks sink through the floor over the last 15% of life (SinkOut).
local SINK_START = 0.85

-- Weak-keyed by burst Model so rig buffers survive pool release/acquire cycles.
local Rigs = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

return function(Particle)

-- Rocks discriminator for the Emit and EmitAnimate dispatch.
function Particle._isRocks(item)
	return item:IsA("BasePart") and item:GetAttribute("IsRocks") == true
end

-- One chunk part cloned from the RT; copyBare strips Transformed children (nested source
-- Part-Icles fire once per burst). Chunks stay ANCHORED; trajectory playback drives their CFrames.
local function buildChunk(rt)

	chunk.Anchored = true
	chunk.CanCollide = false
	chunk.CanQuery = false
	chunk.CanTouch = false
	chunk.Massless = false
	chunk.Locked = true
	chunk.Archivable = false
	chunk.CastShadow = true
	chunk.Transparency = 0
	local decal = chunk:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Decal") or chunk:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Texture")
	return chunk, decal
end

local function chunkCapFor(data)
	return math.clamp(math.floor((data.ChunkCount and data.ChunkCount.Max or 10) + 0.5), 1, MAX_CHUNKS)
end

local function buildRig(data)
	local cap = chunkCapFor(data)
	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = "RockBurst"
	model.Archivable = false
	local rig = {
		chunkCap = cap,
		parts = table.create(cap),
		decals = table.create(cap),
		baseSize = table.create(cap),
		halfExt = table.create(cap),
		bounciness = table.create(cap),
		gravity = table.create(cap),
		friction = table.create(cap),
		launchVel = table.create(cap),
		launchAng = table.create(cap),
		spawnPos = table.create(cap),
		spawnRot = table.create(cap),
		trajs = table.create(cap),
		touched = table.create(cap),
		hitDone = table.create(cap),
		writeCFs = table.create(cap),
	}
	for i = 1, cap do
		local chunk, decal = buildChunk(data.RenderTemplate)
		chunk.Name = "Chunk" .. i
		chunk.CFrame = FAR_CFRAME
		chunk.Parent = model
		rig.parts[i] = chunk
		rig.decals[i] = decal
		rig.baseSize[i] = chunk.Size
		rig.writeCFs[i] = FAR_CFRAME
	end
	Rigs[model] = rig
	return model, rig
end

-- Pool acquire; a foreign, layout-drifted or destroyed-chunk rig is rebuilt.
local function acquireRocks(data)
	local expected = chunkCapFor(data)
	if data.Pool ~= false then
		local model = Pool.acquire(data.RenderTemplate, "Rocks")
		if model then
			local rig = Rigs[model]
			if rig and rig.chunkCap == expected and rig.parts[1] and rig.parts[1].Parent == model then
				model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
				return model, rig
			end
			pcall(function() model:Destroy() end)
		end
	end
	local model, rig = buildRig(data)
	model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	return model, rig
end

-- Step-gated visual write on every chunk and decal; the Scale graph multiplies baseSize.
local function writeVisuals(pData, t)
	local graphs, seeds = pData.Graphs, pData.Seeds
	local trans = graphs.Transparency and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(t, graphs.Transparency, seeds.Transparency) or 0
	if pData.SkipTransparency then trans = pData._curTrans or trans end
	local bright = graphs.Brightness and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(t, graphs.Brightness, seeds.Brightness) or 1
	local color
	if graphs.Color and not pData.SkipColor then
		local c = GraphMod.QueryColorPointWithTime(t, graphs.Color)
		color = Color3.new(math.min(c.R * bright, 1), math.min(c.G * bright, 1), math.min(c.B * bright, 1))
	end
	local scale = graphs.Scale and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(t, graphs.Scale, seeds.Scale)
	local rig = pData._rig
	local scaleChanged = scale and scale ~= pData._curScale
	if scale then pData._curScale = scale end
	pData._curTrans = trans
	-- What the chunks show: a Container's Transparency fades the debris on top of its own.
	local shown = ContainerFade.number(trans, ContainerFade.of(pData._drive))
	for i = 1, rig.chunkCap do
		local chunk = rig.parts[i]
		chunk.Transparency = shown
		if color then chunk.Color = color end
		local decal = rig.decals[i]
		if decal then
			decal.Transparency = shown
			if color then decal.Color3 = color end
		end
		if scaleChanged then
			chunk.Size = rig.baseSize[i] * math.max(scale, 0.01)
		end
	end
end

-- Edit-path raycast params: the makeHitParams filter (source, RT, EmitParent, user OnHit cfg), both
-- engine folders, and RespectCanCollide so rocks pass through non-collidable decoration.
local function buildRockParams(self, pData)
	local p = EventsMod.makeHitParams(pData)
	p.RespectCanCollide = true
	pcall(function()
		p:AddToFilter(self:GetFolder())
		p:AddToFilter(self:GetPoolFolder())
	end)
	pData._rockParams = p
	pData._raycastFn = function(origin, disp)
		return workspace:Raycast(origin, disp, p)
	end
end

-- Build the next `budget` chunk paths (all raycast cost lives here). Running first-impact /
-- rest accumulators finalize once every chunk is built; until then the write gate stays open.
local function buildTrajectories(pData, budget)
	local rig = pData._rig
	local rayFn = pData._raycastFn
	local scale = pData._curScale or 1
	local first = pData._trajBuilt + 1
	local last = math.min(pData._chunkCount, pData._trajBuilt + budget)
	for i = first, last do
		local traj = Trajectory.build(rig.spawnPos[i], rig.launchVel[i], rig.spawnRot[i], rig.launchAng[i],
			rig.halfExt[i], scale, rig.gravity[i], rig.bounciness[i], rig.friction[i], rayFn)
		rig.trajs[i] = traj
		if traj.impactT and traj.impactT < pData._firstImpactT then
			pData._firstImpactT = traj.impactT
			pData._firstHitInfo = traj.hit
		end
		-- A chunk that never rests (no ground in reach) keeps the write gate open: latching at the max
		-- finite rest would freeze it mid-air.
		if traj.restT == math.huge then
			pData._trajAnyEndless = true
		elseif traj.restT > pData._trajMaxRest then
			pData._trajMaxRest = traj.restT
		end
	end
	pData._trajBuilt = last
	if last >= pData._chunkCount then
		pData._maxRestT = (pData._trajMaxRest > 0 and not pData._trajAnyEndless) and pData._trajMaxRest or math.huge
	end
end

-- Per-burst path setup, shared by Emit / Animate / loop refresh: every chunk starts on a
-- ballistic placeholder, the first budget of real paths lands now, Update builds the rest.
local function startPhysics(self, pData)
	buildRockParams(self, pData)
	local rig = pData._rig
	pData._trajBuilt = 0
	pData._firstImpactT = math.huge
	pData._firstHitInfo = nil
	pData._trajMaxRest = 0
	pData._trajAnyEndless = false
	pData._maxRestT = math.huge
	pData._restWritten = false
	pData._hitsPending = pData._hitPerChunk and pData._chunkCount or 0
	for i = 1, pData._chunkCount do
		rig.trajs[i] = Trajectory.ballistic(rig.spawnPos[i], rig.launchVel[i], rig.spawnRot[i], rig.launchAng[i])
		rig.hitDone[i] = false
	end
	buildTrajectories(pData, TRAJ_BUILD_BUDGET)
end

local function fireChunkHit(self, pData, hit)
	local payload = EventsMod.makePayload(self, pData, "OnHit", nil)
	payload.HitInstance = hit.Instance
	payload.Other = hit.Instance
	payload.HitPosition = hit.Position
	payload.HitNormal = hit.Normal
	EventsMod.fire(self, pData, "OnHit", pData.EventChainCtx, payload)
end

function Particle:EmitRocks(item, link, emitCtx)
	if not item or not item.Parent then return end
	local data = self:GetEmitData(item, emitCtx)
	if not data or not data.RenderTemplate then return end

	local lifeTime = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Lifetime)
	if lifeTime <= 0 then lifeTime = 0.001 end

	local model, rig = acquireRocks(data)
	local pData = PDataBuilder.build(item, data, model, rig, lifeTime, emitCtx, link)

	Particle._seedTsOverride(pData, item)
	if data.Pool ~= false then
		pData._sourceRT, pData._poolKind = data.RenderTemplate, "Rocks"
	end
	-- Carried by a Matte: the chunks are windows in its layer (Matte/init).
	self:_matteCarry(emitCtx, pData, rig.parts)

	writeVisuals(pData, 0)
	model.Parent = data.EmitParent or self:GetFolder()
	startPhysics(self, pData)
	Pool.restoreTrails(model, "Rocks")
	ParticlesMod.EnableEmit(model, self:_makeAliveCheck())

	pData._nestedAlive = { true }
	self:_registerEmit(pData, emitCtx)
	NestedEmit.walk(self, data.RenderTemplate, model, pData._nestedAlive, emitCtx)
end

-- Animate mode: singleton looping burst per source (fresh rig, never pooled).
function Particle:EmitRocksAnimate(item, link, emitCtx)
	if not item or not item.Parent then return end
	if self.ActiveAnimates[item] then return end
	local data = self:GetEmitData(item, emitCtx)
	if not data or not data.RenderTemplate then return end

	local lifeTime = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Lifetime)
	if lifeTime <= 0 then lifeTime = 0.001 end

	local model, rig = buildRig(data)
	model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	local pData = PDataBuilder.build(item, data, model, rig, lifeTime, emitCtx, link)
	pData.IsAnimate = true
	pData.AnimateItem = item
	pData._animateLink = link

	Particle._seedTsOverride(pData, item)
	writeVisuals(pData, 0)
	model.Parent = data.EmitParent or self:GetFolder()
	startPhysics(self, pData)
	ParticlesMod.EnableEmit(model, self:_makeAliveCheck())

	pData._nestedAlive = { true }
	self.ActiveAnimates[item] = pData
	self:_registerEmit(pData, emitCtx)
	NestedEmit.walk(self, data.RenderTemplate, model, pData._nestedAlive, emitCtx)
end

-- Per-frame update: evaluate the predetermined paths at effective time (any
-- Timescale, any direction) + one BulkMoveTo; idles once everything is at rest.
function Particle:UpdateRocks(pData, dt, currentTime)
	local real_i = math.min(math.max((currentTime - pData.StartTime) / pData.LifeTime, 0), 1)
	local ts
	if pData._tsOverride ~= nil and currentTime < (pData._tsOverrideUntil or 0) then
		ts = pData._tsOverride
	else
		ts = pData.Graphs.Timescale and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(real_i, pData.Graphs.Timescale, pData.Seeds.Timescale) or 1
	end
	local dtTs = dt * ts
	local lifeTime = pData.LifeTime
	local newEff = (pData._effectiveElapsed or 0) + (pData._timeFrozen and 0 or dtTs)
	if newEff < 0 then newEff = 0 end
	if newEff > lifeTime then newEff = lifeTime end
	pData._effectiveElapsed = newEff

	local model = pData.VisualPart
	if not model or not model.Parent then return true end
	if pData.TotalKeyFrames <= 0 then return true end
	local isDying = real_i >= 1 and (newEff >= lifeTime or newEff <= 0)

	if not isDying then
		local rig = pData._rig
		if pData._trajBuilt < pData._chunkCount then buildTrajectories(pData, TRAJ_BUILD_BUDGET) end
		local sinkPhase = pData._sinkOut and (newEff / lifeTime) > SINK_START
		if newEff < pData._maxRestT or sinkPhase or not pData._restWritten then
			local sinkEase = 0
			if sinkPhase then
				local e = ((newEff / lifeTime) - SINK_START) / (1 - SINK_START)
				sinkEase = e * e
			end
			for i = 1, pData._chunkCount do
				local traj = rig.trajs[i]
				if traj then
					local cf = Trajectory.evaluate(traj, newEff, rig.gravity[i])
					if sinkEase > 0 and newEff > traj.restT then
						-- Buried along the rest normal: the largest scaled dimension x 1.5 clears the surface.
						local sz = rig.baseSize[i]
						local depth = math.max(sz.X, sz.Y, sz.Z) * math.max(pData._curScale or 1, 0.01) * 1.5
						cf = cf.Rotation + (cf.Position - (traj.restNormal or Vector3.yAxis) * (depth * sinkEase))
					end
					rig.writeCFs[i] = cf
					-- InheritFloor lands the moment the path says it does.
					if pData._inheritFloor and not rig.touched[i] and traj.impactT and newEff >= traj.impactT and traj.hit then
						rig.touched[i] = true
						local part = rig.parts[i]
						pcall(function()
							part.Material = traj.hit.Instance.Material
							part.Color = traj.hit.Instance.Color
						end)
						pData.SkipColor = true
					end
				end
			end
			workspace:BulkMoveTo(rig.parts, rig.writeCFs, Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged)
			-- One flush past rest, then idle until sink or reversed time.
			pData._restWritten = newEff >= pData._maxRestT and not sinkPhase
		end
		-- OnHit from the precomputed impacts: once per burst at the earliest, or per chunk.
		if pData.Events and pData.Events.OnHit then
			if pData._hitPerChunk then
				if pData._hitsPending > 0 then
					for i = 1, pData._chunkCount do
						local traj = rig.trajs[i]
						if not rig.hitDone[i] and traj.impactT and traj.hit and newEff >= traj.impactT then
							rig.hitDone[i] = true
							pData._hitsPending -= 1
							fireChunkHit(self, pData, traj.hit)
						end
					end
				end
			elseif not pData._hitFired and pData._trajBuilt >= pData._chunkCount
				and pData._firstHitInfo and newEff >= pData._firstImpactT then
				pData._hitFired = true
				fireChunkHit(self, pData, pData._firstHitInfo)
			end
		end
	end

	local targetStep = math.floor(math.min(math.max(newEff / lifeTime, 0), 1) * pData.TotalKeyFrames)
	if targetStep ~= pData.CurrentStep then
		pData.CurrentStep = targetStep
		writeVisuals(pData, targetStep / pData.TotalKeyFrames)
	end

	return isDying
end

-- AnimateLoop per-cycle refresh (EngineReplay dispatch): re-roll every chunk from
-- the source's CURRENT pose, rebuild paths, restart physics; rebuild the rig on
-- layout change.
function Particle:_refreshRocksAnimate(pData, freshData)
	-- Generic replay assigns pData.Link from freshData; Rocks never links post-emit.
	pData.Link = nil
	pData._sinkOut = freshData.SinkOut ~= false
	pData._inheritFloor = freshData.InheritFloor == true
	pData._hitPerChunk = freshData.HitPerChunk == true
	pData._hitFired = false
	pData.SkipColor = nil

	local expected = chunkCapFor(freshData)
	if expected ~= pData._rig.chunkCap and freshData.RenderTemplate then
		local oldModel = pData.VisualPart
		local parent = oldModel and oldModel.Parent
		local model, rig = buildRig(freshData)
		model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
		pData.VisualPart = model
		pData._rig = rig
		model.Parent = parent or self:GetFolder()
		if oldModel then pcall(function() oldModel:Destroy() end) end
	end

	local originCF = PDataBuilder.cloneOrigin(pData, pData._animateLink)
	local src = pData.AnimateItem
	if not originCF and src and src.Parent then originCF = src.CFrame end
	-- Rebuilt rigs need the same WorldPivot stamp PDataBuilder.build gives fresh ones.
	if originCF then pcall(function() pData.VisualPart.WorldPivot = originCF end) end

	local rig = pData._rig
	PDataBuilder.rollChunks(pData, freshData, rig, originCF or CFrame.new())
	writeVisuals(pData, 0)
	startPhysics(self, pData)
end

end
